subject: Production latency spike — Bridgewater checkout affecting inference requests
messages:
From: Mike Sullivan <mike.sullivan@bridgewaterretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@bridgewaterretail.com
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High latency & 5xx surge on checkout — Redwood inference calls

Marissa —

We started seeing a sharp increase in end-to-end latency and 5xx rates for Redwood inference calls during our afternoon checkout spike (~09:00 PDT). Error rate jumped from ~0.3% to ~6% and p95 latency rose from ~210ms to ~1.8s. Impacting user conversions.

Attached is a traceroute and sample request IDs (in the CSV). Can your team take a look? We believe something changed in the peering path between our VPC and Redwood's inference gateway — but happy to assist.

Mike
Mike Sullivan
SRE Lead, Bridgewater Retail
mike.sullivan@bridgewaterretail.com

Cc: Mike Sullivan <mike.sullivan@bridgewaterretail.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: High latency & 5xx surge on checkout — Redwood inference calls

Team — forwarding incident from Bridgewater. Quick summary: spike at ~09:00 PDT with higher 5xx and p95 latency for their inference routes. Customer included traceroute + request IDs. Asking for urgent triage; their SRE is standing by.

Can Eng network and infra take initial look (naomi/vivek)? Karhtik, can you coordinate with CS on temporary fallbacks (dedicated pool or model variant) while we diagnose? I want an internal triage note and an exec summary if this needs leadership attention.

Goal: confirm whether this is on our egress/peering or on Bridgewater path and propose immediate mitigations.

- Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

[attachment: peer-metrics-20260616.csv (csv)]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: High latency & 5xx surge on checkout — Redwood inference calls

Marissa / team — initial findings from a quick look at the customer's traceroute and our egress metrics:

- The traceroute shows asymmetric hops at AS701 (their cloud provider edge) with repeated TTL increases between hop 6 and 8. Packet loss ~3-4% on that segment.
- Our egress telemetry (peer_metrics) shows a short-lived spike in TCP retransmits and SYN retries to Bridgewater's prefix starting 08:58 PDT and lasting ~22 minutes.
- DNS: customer's service is resolving our inference-gw host to a different egress IP in a minority of their requests; TTLs on their resolver are low (30s), which may be increasing DNS churn during the checkout burst.
- We also observed elevated 503s from our proxy fleet in us-west-2 that align with the customer's timestamps. Proxy logs show connection resets to one downstream NAT cluster.

Preliminary hypothesis: combination of transient peering route oscillation and their aggressive resolver TTL causing uneven routing to a subset of our proxies where a NAT peer was overloaded — resulting in retries and 5xx. Not a pure application regression.

Immediate asks:
1) Can CS schedule an immediate brief maintenance window / traffic cutover from the affected prefix to an alternate peering adjacency? (this would require coordination with Bridgewater's networking team)
2) We'll spin a canary route bypass (bypass the affected NAT cluster) and monitor for 15 minutes.
3) Engineering needs permission to initiate emergency route preference change and to update the gateway DNS mapping to favor the healthy egress IP while we stabilize.

I'll attach the raw traces and a quick graph of retransmits. If we get permission I'll open INF-4821 with detailed telemetry and rollback plan.

— Naomi
Sr. Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

[attachment: raw-traces-bridgewater-20260616.tgz (text)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec: Bridgewater checkout outage candidate — recommended mitigation and ETO

Marissa / Leadership — short exec summary and ask: we are seeing a customer-impacting latency and error surge tied to a peering path instability plus resolver churn on the customer's side. Impact: Bridgewater checkout throughput degraded; they reported conversion regressions.

Recommendation (immediate):
- Approve emergency traffic steering for Bridgewater prefixes to our alternate peering adjacency (eta to flip ~6 min, rollback <3 min). This requires us to push a route-preference update at the edge and temporarily bias DNS to healthy egress IPs for that customer.
- Enable temporary dedicated capacity for Bridgewater (small reserved pool) for the next 24 hours to reduce compounding queue pressure on shared proxies. Cost impact: estimated $2.5k for 24h for requested capacity.
- Notify Sales/CS to tell the customer we are executing a cross-team fix and request permission for a 15-minute cutover window at 12:00 PDT.

If approved I will execute the route preference change and monitor via INF-4821; Naomi will validate egress health and watch for retransmit decrease. We should brief the CTO if the fix does not reduce errors in 30 minutes.

- Vivek
VP, Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

[attachment: fallback-routing-plan.pdf (pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Sullivan <mike.sullivan@bridgewaterretail.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: High latency & 5xx surge on checkout — Redwood inference calls

Mike — thanks for the quick data. We took the following actions after internal triage:

1) At 12:00 PDT on 2026-06-16 we executed an emergency traffic steering to an alternate peering adjacency and biased DNS mapping to the healthy egress IP.
2) We provisioned a small dedicated pool for your production inference traffic for 24h to absorb bursty checkout traffic.
3) Naomi validated that TCP retransmits dropped from ~3.5% to ~0.2% within 7 minutes of the cutover; proxy 503s returned to baseline and p95 latency for the sampled request IDs dropped to ~220ms.

Next steps:
- Please confirm whether you can increase your resolver TTL to >= 120s to reduce churn during spikes; we can coordinate with your network team.
- We'll keep the dedicated capacity for 24 hours and then run a canary rollback; we'll open a follow-up postmortem in INF-4821.

Appreciate your patience — we're keeping a pager on this and will share the postmortem with remediation items.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
